title: October 21: Jäännös, the real GPT-2 residue-routing kill
summary: Jäännös turns Sihti-style core/residue separation into an activation-aware banded GPT-2 MLP with cheap local sketches of omitted contributions. The full real-model GPU receipt (8192 WikiText-2 evaluation positions, 24 routed matrices) validates reconstructability and some nonrandom allocation information, but the preregistered G4 local-compute advantage is KILL: fixed uniform rank wins at every matched theoretical MLP-operation budget. Exact residue norms given free still lose. No wall-clock speedup was measured; the full-factor forward computes then masks, and the global-margin alternative substitutes precomputed dense logits. The original user-provided machine-readable receipt is preserved under data/audits; atlas review did not rerun the GPU experiment.

nodes.claim: A frozen GPT-2 experiment splits each of 24 MLP matrices into a rank-256 core, sparse outlier weights and eight 64-rank residue bands. Per-token, per-matrix 4-row sketches estimate remaining band output norm and propose a locally adaptive compute budget, tested against fixed-rank, exact-tail, shuffled and global-margin attackers.
nodes.survived: All bands reconstruct GPT-2 weights to maximum relative error 3.18e-13; theoretical sketch multiply-adds cost 2.604% of the dense routed MLPs. Local sketch allocation beats the same-cost randomly permuted k-arrays at 0.6/0.7/0.8/0.9 budgets (40.54/48.40/57.41/68.00% versus 37.50/43.43/50.96/61.41% dense top-1 agreement). This is a nonrandom local signal, not a winning compute policy.
nodes.killed: Preregistered GPT-2 G4 KILL: at theoretical MLP budgets 0.6/0.7/0.8/0.9, uniform fixed rank reaches 53.66/62.53/70.10/76.62% agreement versus local sketch 40.54/48.40/57.41/68.00%. The free exact-tail norm rule also loses (41.42/50.36/60.19/71.51%). Full-rank factorization costs 1.25x dense; high local fidelity costs more than dense. Per-token masked computation and sparse outlier application are not efficient kernels; global-margin has precomputed dense-logit assistance and is not realizable as evaluated. No actual GPU speedup or general no-go theorem.
nodes.era: October 21: residue magnitude is not decision value

edges.why: Jäännös states that the proposed per-compartment local difficulty gate and earlier Sihti hidden-state/residue discussion motivated its per-token band selection; the connection is conceptual, not code inheritance.

Both test how cheaply measured local signal magnitude relates to the value of an additional observation/computation. Jäännös makes the discrepancy explicit on a pretrained language model; this is a conceptual recurrence, not direct derivation.

motifs.title: Residue size is not the value of a decision
motifs.description: An exact core/residue representation and a cheap norm sketch do not identify which omitted directions change downstream answers. On GPT-2, a per-token norm-based router allocates nonrandomly and still loses to fixed rank at every registered cost. Information magnitude, causal consequence and useful budget allocation remain distinct.
